title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: Oblate 4f density (for example Nd3+, Tb3+, Dy3+) is stabilized by an axial crystal field, whereas prolate density (for example Er3+) is stabilized by an equatorial field; the preferred geometry therefore follows the mJ electron-density shape.
explanation: The review adopts the Rinehart–Long electrostatic classification as a design rule to maximize anisotropy by matching ligand arrangement to the angular 4f density. It explicitly notes that the classification is mJ-dependent: Yb3+ has a prolate mJ = ±7/2 state but a largely oblate mJ = ±5/2 state.
scope: Ln3+ SMMs designed by crystal-field electrostatics.
conditions: Ligand geometry chosen to match the ground (and relevant excited) mJ density.
caveats: The simple oblate/prolate assignment is not universal for every mJ level of a given ion, as illustrated for Yb3+.
evidence_locations: Section 3.4 for equatorial design of prolate Er3+
